newsitem.title: UK: Medeva says acquires cancer drug rights.
newsitem.headline: Medeva says acquires cancer drug rights.

text.p: British pharmaceuticals group Medeva Plc said on Wednesday it had acquired marketing rights in the U.S. to a drug being developed for bladder cancer by Anthra Pharmaceuticals Inc.
In a statement Medeva said it would also acquire a one percent stake in Anthra.

Medeva will pay Anthra a total of around $8 million in development and licensing fees, plus $2.1 million for production of three batches of the drug and a total of $16 million for approval of the drug in two separate forms of bladder cancer. It will also pay royalties on any sales.
Medeva said Anthra planned to seek a regulatory approval for the drug, AD32, in refractory carcinoma-in-situ of the bladder in the final quarter of 1997.
A second application for papillary bladder cancer, which accounts for around 80 percent of new bladder cancers in the U.S, is planned for early 1999.
